title: Spatial correlation modeling of environmental extremes with HazardMaps
text: HazardMaps provides unified workflow spatial dependence modeling environmental extremes — raw gridded datasets spatially coherent pseudoscenarios. package supports regular longitude-latitude grids (e.g. ERA5, Copernicus) rotated curvilinear grids (e.g. EURO-CORDEX) without change user interface. Example dataset. vignette uses daily maximum wind-gust speed Northeast Italy running example. workflow applies unchanged gridded environmental variable: precipitation, temperature, wave height, etc. package developed part research presented Clavijo Mesa et al. (2026a, 2026b), whose datasets included built-example files. Users need prepare raw Copernicus EURO-CORDEX downloads using package can find helper R scripts inst/scripts/, accessible via system.file("scripts", package = "HazardMaps"). Two datasets used throughout: Copernicus — regular longitude-latitude grid, ERA5-based, 195 cells, 1994–2021 EURO-CORDEX — rotated curvilinear grid, RCM simulation, 1872 cells (1568 land), 1970–2005 workflow seven steps: Ingest prepare data Select extreme-event days Fit marginal distributions Estimate spatial dependence Fit copula stochastic field models Simulate pseudoscenarios Validate cluster-size statistics
code: library(HazardMaps)

title: Spatial correlation modeling of environmental extremes with HazardMaps
text: starting point CF-convention NetCDF file. hm_read_netcdf() reads detects grid type automatically — configuration needed. hm_standardize_coords() flattens coordinate arrays single data.frame one row per grid cell — format downstream functions expect. hm_decode_time() converts CF-style time values (e.g. “days since 1970-01-01”) R Date objects. hm_plot_spatial_domain() visualises study area. draws correct cell geometry automatically — straight lines regular grids, curvilinear lines rotated grids. Copernicus regular grid domain. EURO-CORDEX rotated grid domain.
code: wind_cop <- hm_read_netcdf(   system.file("extdata", "Copernicus_dailymax_1994_2021.nc",               package = "HazardMaps"),   var = "i10fg" )  wind_euc <- hm_read_netcdf(   system.file("extdata", "EuroCordex_wsgsmax_1970_2005.nc",               package = "HazardMaps"),   var = "wsgsmax" )  wind_cop$meta$grid_type #> [1] "regular" wind_euc$meta$grid_type #> [1] "rotated" wind_cop <- hm_standardize_coords(wind_cop) wind_cop <- hm_decode_time(wind_cop) wind_cop <- hm_get_grid_geometry(wind_cop)  wind_euc <- hm_standardize_coords(wind_euc) wind_euc <- hm_decode_time(wind_euc) wind_euc <- hm_get_grid_geometry(wind_euc)  cat("Copernicus: ", nrow(wind_cop$coords), "cells |",     length(wind_cop$time), "days\n") #> Copernicus:  195 cells | 10226 days cat("EURO-CORDEX:", nrow(wind_euc$coords), "cells |",     length(wind_euc$time), "days\n") #> EURO-CORDEX: 1872 cells | 13149 days hm_plot_spatial_domain(wind_cop, dataset = "copernicus",                        title = "Copernicus domain", show_map = TRUE) hm_plot_spatial_domain(wind_euc, dataset = "eurocordex",                        title = "EURO-CORDEX domain", show_map = TRUE)

title: Spatial correlation modeling of environmental extremes with HazardMaps
text: days least one grid cell threshold kept. Everything threshold noise dependence modeling purposes. hm_plot_exceedance() maps often cell exceeded threshold full period. Exceedance count — Copernicus. Exceedance count — EURO-CORDEX. hm_plot_exceedance_time() shows whether frequency extreme events changes observation period. Extreme-event days per year — Copernicus. Extreme-event days per decade — EURO-CORDEX.
code: wind_cop_ext <- hm_select_extreme_events(wind_cop, threshold = 25) wind_euc_ext <- hm_select_extreme_events(wind_euc, threshold = 25)  cat("Copernicus: ", wind_cop_ext$meta$filter$n_days_retained,     "extreme-event days out of", wind_cop_ext$meta$filter$n_days_original, "\n") #> Copernicus:  382 extreme-event days out of 10226 cat("EURO-CORDEX:", wind_euc_ext$meta$filter$n_days_retained,     "extreme-event days out of", wind_euc_ext$meta$filter$n_days_original, "\n") #> EURO-CORDEX: 5635 extreme-event days out of 13149 hm_plot_exceedance(wind_cop, threshold = 25, metric = "count",                    dataset = "copernicus", show_map = TRUE,                    title = "Wind-gust exceedance count — Copernicus") hm_plot_exceedance(wind_euc, threshold = 25, metric = "count",                    dataset = "eurocordex", show_map = TRUE,                    title = "Wind-gust exceedance count — EURO-CORDEX") hm_plot_exceedance_time(wind_cop, threshold = 25, by = "year",                         title = "Extreme-event days per year — Copernicus") hm_plot_exceedance_time(wind_euc, threshold = 25, by = "decade",                         title = "Extreme-event days per decade — EURO-CORDEX")

title: Spatial correlation modeling of environmental extremes with HazardMaps
text: estimating spatial dependence, cell needs marginal distribution. separates marginal behavior dependence structure — standard approach multivariate extreme-value analysis. hm_to_matrix() reshapes data time--cell matrix. hm_filter_land_cells() removes columns valid data — mandatory EURO-CORDEX, whose domain includes sea cells. hm_fit_marginals() fits six candidate families cell maximum likelihood selects best BIC. six families : Weibull, Gamma, Lognormal, Gumbel, Zero-truncated Gaussian, Zero-truncated Laplace. look . Weibull dominates datasets — expected wind-gust extremes. spatial map shows cells deviate Weibull : coastal cells Alpine valleys tend favour Gamma Zero-truncated Gaussian due different tail behavior. Best-fitting distribution cell — Copernicus. Best-fitting distribution cell — EURO-CORDEX. Frequency best-fitting families across cells. Frequency best-fitting families across cells. Probability Integral Transform (PIT) converts observation uniform scale using fitted CDF, Gaussian scores via probit transform. Gaussian scores (Z) feed spatial dependence estimation; uniform values (U) feed copula.
code:
obs_cop <- hm_to_matrix(wind_cop_ext) obs_euc <- hm_to_matrix(wind_euc_ext)  obs_cop <- hm_filter_land_cells(obs_cop) obs_euc <- hm_filter_land_cells(obs_euc)  cat("Copernicus matrix :", nrow(obs_cop), "days x", ncol(obs_cop), "cells
") #> Copernicus matrix : 382 days x 195 cells cat("EURO-CORDEX matrix:", nrow(obs_euc), "days x", ncol(obs_euc), "cells
") #> EURO-CORDEX matrix: 5635 days x 1568 cells marginals_cop <- hm_fit_marginals(obs_cop, criterion = "bic") marginals_euc <- hm_fit_marginals(obs_euc, criterion = "bic") cat("Copernicus — best distribution per cell:
") #> Copernicus — best distribution per cell: print(sort(table(marginals_cop$best_dist), decreasing = TRUE)) #>  #> weibull   gamma   tnorm   lnorm  gumbel  #>     124      44      17       9       1  cat("
EURO-CORDEX — best distribution per cell:
") #>  #> EURO-CORDEX — best distribution per cell: print(sort(table(marginals_euc$best_dist), decreasing = TRUE)) #>  #>  weibull    tnorm    gamma    lnorm tlaplace  #>     1138      284      112       23       11 hm_plot_best_dist(wind_cop_ext, marginals_cop,                   title = "Best-fitting marginal — Copernicus",                   show_map = TRUE) wind_euc_land        <- wind_euc_ext wind_euc_land$coords <- attr(obs_euc, "coords")  hm_plot_best_dist(wind_euc_land, marginals_euc,                   title = "Best-fitting marginal — EURO-CORDEX",                   show_map = TRUE) hm_plot_dist_frequency(marginals_cop,                        title = "Distribution frequency — Copernicus") hm_plot_dist_frequency(marginals_euc,                        title = "Distribution frequency — EURO-CORDEX") pit_cop <- hm_pit_transform(obs_cop, marginals_cop) pit_euc <- hm_pit_transform(obs_euc, marginals_euc)  cat("Copernicus — cells transformed:", pit_cop$n_cells_ok,     "| skipped:", pit_cop$n_cells_skipped, "
") #> Copernicus — cells transformed: 195 | skipped: 0 cat("EURO-CORDEX — cells transformed:", pit_euc$n_cells_ok,     "| skipped:", pit_euc$n_cells_skipped, "
") #> EURO-CORDEX — cells transformed: 1568 | skipped: 0

title: Spatial correlation modeling of environmental extremes with HazardMaps
text: empirical spatial correlation measured Kendall’s τ, rank-based assume distribution data. hm_distance_matrix() computes great-circle distance kilometres every pair cells. hm_empirical_kendall() estimates pairwise Kendall correlation Gaussian scores. Computational note. large grids (> 500 cells), computing N(N-1)/2 pairs expensive. Use cell_idx pass representative subsample — done EURO-CORDEX. hm_empirical_correlogram() bins pairwise correlations distance produce smooth summary correlation decays separation. Empirical spatial correlogram datasets. Empirical spatial correlogram datasets. Interpretation. Correlation highest short distances (~0.75–0.80) decreases steadily increasing separation, reaching near-zero beyond 250–300 km. pattern confirms strong local spatial dependence weak long-range dependence — consistent synoptic-scale windstorm events affect areas 50–200 km.
code: distances_cop <- hm_distance_matrix(attr(obs_cop, "coords")) kendall_cop   <- hm_empirical_kendall(pit_cop$Z)  land_idx      <- which(!is.na(marginals_euc$best_dist))[1:50] distances_euc <- hm_distance_matrix(attr(obs_euc, "coords")[land_idx, ]) kendall_euc   <- hm_empirical_kendall(pit_euc$Z, cell_idx = land_idx) corg_cop <- hm_empirical_correlogram(kendall_cop, distances_cop, n_bins = 20) corg_euc <- hm_empirical_correlogram(kendall_euc, distances_euc, n_bins = 15) hm_plot_correlogram(corg_cop,                     title = "Empirical correlogram — Copernicus") hm_plot_correlogram(corg_euc,                     title = "Empirical correlogram — EURO-CORDEX (50-cell subsample)")

title: Spatial correlation modeling of environmental extremes with HazardMaps
text: Vine copulas decompose joint distribution cells cascade bivariate copulas. Three structures available: C-vine (one central node drives others), D-vine (chain structure), Gaussian (elliptical baseline).
code: uniform_small   <- pit_cop$U[, 1:30] marginals_small <- marginals_cop[1:30, ]  copula_cvine <- hm_fit_copula(uniform_small, type = "cvine") copula_dvine <- hm_fit_copula(uniform_small, type = "dvine") copula_gauss <- hm_fit_copula(uniform_small, type = "gaussian")  cat("Cells:", copula_cvine$n_cells,     "| Observations:", copula_cvine$n_obs, "\n") #> Cells: 30 | Observations: 382

title: Spatial correlation modeling of environmental extremes with HazardMaps
text: model generates matrix synthetic extreme-event fields. Every row one spatially coherent scenario — plausible simultaneous wind-gust intensity grid cells.
code:
scenarios_cvine <- hm_simulate_copula(copula_cvine, marginals_small,                                        n_scenarios = 500L, seed = 42L) scenarios_dvine <- hm_simulate_copula(copula_dvine, marginals_small,                                        n_scenarios = 500L, seed = 42L) scenarios_gauss <- hm_simulate_copula(copula_gauss, marginals_small,                                        n_scenarios = 500L, seed = 42L)  cat("Copula scenarios — dimensions:", dim(scenarios_cvine)[1], "x",     dim(scenarios_cvine)[2], "
") #> Copula scenarios — dimensions: 500 x 30 cat("Value range: [",     round(min(scenarios_cvine, na.rm = TRUE), 2), ",",     round(max(scenarios_cvine, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "] m/s
") #> Value range: [ 2.22 , 41.62 ] m/s scenarios_sf <- hm_simulate_sf_kle(   sf_model_cop, distances_cop, marginals_cop,   n_scenarios = 500L, var_retain = 0.95, seed = 42L )  cat("SF scenarios — dimensions:", dim(scenarios_sf)[1], "x",     dim(scenarios_sf)[2], "
") #> SF scenarios — dimensions: 500 x 195 cat("KLE modes retained:", attr(scenarios_sf, "k_modes"),     "| Variance explained:", round(attr(scenarios_sf, "var_explained"), 3), "
") #> KLE modes retained: 165 | Variance explained: 0.951 cat("Value range: [",     round(min(scenarios_sf, na.rm = TRUE), 2), ",",     round(max(scenarios_sf, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "] m/s
") #> Value range: [ 0.98 , 43.97 ] m/s

title: Spatial Dependence Modeling and Pseudoscenario Generation for Natural Hazards
text: HazardMaps R package reproducible spatial dependence analysis natural hazards. provides unified workflow ingest gridded climate datasets, fit compare spatial dependence models, generate spatially coherent pseudoscenarios uncertainty quantification. package implements methodology Clavijo Mesa et al. (2026), validated wind-gust extremes Northeast Italy using Copernicus EURO-CORDEX reanalysis data.

title: Spatial Dependence Modeling and Pseudoscenario Generation for Natural Hazards

title: Spatial Dependence Modeling and Pseudoscenario Generation for Natural Hazards
code: library(HazardMaps)  # 1. Ingest x <- hm_read_netcdf("Copernicus_dailymax.nc", var = "i10fg") x <- hm_standardize_coords(x) x <- hm_decode_time(x)  # 2. Filter extreme events x_ext <- hm_select_extreme_events(x, threshold = 25) X     <- hm_to_matrix(x_ext) X     <- hm_filter_land_cells(X)  # 3. Fit marginal distributions fits <- hm_fit_marginals(X, criterion = "bic") pit  <- hm_pit_transform(X, fits)  # 4. Estimate spatial dependence D    <- hm_distance_matrix(attr(X, "coords")) tau  <- hm_empirical_kendall(pit$Z) corg <- hm_empirical_correlogram(tau, D)  # 5a. Copula model (C-vine, D-vine, or Gaussian) cop       <- hm_fit_copula(pit$U, type = "cvine") scenarios <- hm_simulate_copula(cop, fits, n_scenarios = 1000)  # 5b. Stochastic field model (KLE-based) model     <- hm_fit_correlation_model(corg) scenarios <- hm_simulate_sf_kle(model, D, fits, n_scenarios = 1000)
